thread:
DeployBot: Starting canary rollout wave-3 -> model=redwood-rt-3b region=us-east batch=5% nodes=[canary-01, canary-02, canary-03] cid=wave-3

IncidentBot: ALERT: canary 'wave-3' elevated 5xx rate (12% 60s window). Health probes failing on 2/3 hosts. Paging eng-oncall.

maya: saw the alert, jumping in. grafana shows heartbeat failures from canary-02 around 11:07:12. p95 latency up.

liam: grabbing recent logs from canary-02, looks like repeated KV cache read errors followed by backend 503s. snippet: `2026-03-11T11:07:09Z ERROR kvcache: read shard 4: EOF`

jordan: thanks, @liam. can you post the short `kubectl logs` tail? i want to see the crash loop or oom info. paging @chen (next shift) for handoff if we escalate.

liam: pasted tail below:
```
[11:06:58] INFO accept request id=... route=/v1/generate
[11:07:09] ERROR kvcache: read shard 4: EOF
[11:07:09] WARN inference: kvcache-miss-stall=120ms
[11:07:10] ERROR http: handler returned 503 internal backend error
[11:07:11] ERROR health: probe failed, last_ok=2026-03-11T11:05:45Z
```

maya: looks like heartbeat sliding window - probe threshold tripped. this meets our canary abort criteria (5xx > 10% for 1m). recommending immediate abort and model fallback.

amanda: customer-impact check: we’re only serving canary traffic (5%); some internal users and a small set of prod traffic routed to canary — estimate ~2% of overall traffic. notify support tier1 to watch for P1?

jordan: agreed. initiating emergency abort for the canary. actions: 1) flip kill-switch for wave-3 feature flag 2) remove canary nodes from LB 3) rollback deployment if needed.

maya: command to flip feature flag (internal tooling):
```
releases feature-flag set kill_wave_3 true --reason="health-abort-5xx" --by=maya
```

jordan: taking LB out of rotation:
```
for n in canary-01 canary-02 canary-03; do cloudctl lb drain $n --timeout=30s; done
```

liam: started draining canary-02, connections draining now. 503 rate dipping.

IncidentBot: ACTION: kill flag flipped by maya at 2026-03-11T11:08:02Z. Traffic routed off canary.

maya: because we changed a kvcache optimization in this rollout, leaning toward rollback to previous revision. jordan, you want to issue `kubectl rollout undo` or keep as is and patch?

jordan: undoing rollout to revision=41 (pre-wave-3) now:
```
kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-serving -n prod --to-revision=41
```

liam: rollback started, pods terminating and recreating. canary-02 logs show 503s stopping. p95 latency returning to baseline.

amanda: alerting CS and support: small fraction (2%) saw elevated errors, we have no high-severity customer reports yet. sending pinned status update to #customers-affected. :white_check_mark:

chen: I’m online, picking up the handoff. will monitor for 15m and then pass to next oncall if stable. what’s the postmortem owner?

maya: @chen thanks. I’ll own follow-up: create INC-2026-0311, include rollout artifacts, kvcache change, and canary metrics. action items: (1) verify kvcache fix and add extra probe ok window (2) add automated rollback runbook step to LB drain before feature flag flip (3) add canary-specific alert to rate-limit noisy probe windows.

jordan: notes for incident timeline logged. next steps: watch SLO for 60m, if any residual 5xx traces -> re-escalate.

liam: quick note — reproducer locally: toggling kvcache patch causes ~30-120ms stall on some shards under load. will open PR with guard and tests.

maya: thanks team. closing live mitigation. final status: canary aborted, rollback initiated, customer impact minimal (estimated 2% requests, no confirmed P1s). will sync in tomorrow's postmortem. :heavy_check_mark:
